title: NVLink persistent link-flap — exploratory notes & rollback checklist
incident_summary: Overnight we observed repeated NVLink link state flaps on a subset of DGX-like nodes (gpu-cc-14/15/18). Symptoms: transient ECC upticks on peer GPUs, occasional driver watchdog resets, and sporadic kernel oops leading to kubelet evictions for pods using all GPUs. Pattern appears tied to sustained high inter-GPU traffic (large attention-model serving bursts) and coincides with firmware churn after last maintenance window.
timeline: 2025-12-05 00:12 - first NVLink alert (prometheus nvlink_link_state_change) on gpu-cc-15; 00:15 - second alert; 00:22 - nvidia-driver watchdog reset observed on gpu-cc-14; 00:40 - operator drained gpu-cc-15 and moved jobs; 01:05 - manual nvlink rescan and nvlink error counters cleared; 01:30 - kernel oops on gpu-cc-18, kubelet evicted pods; 02:10 - rolling restart of driver on gpu-cc-14/18; 05:00 - traffic shifted to other cells, errors subsided; impact: ~3h degraded capacity for high-throughput inference routes.
diagnostics: Metrics looked like: ECC single-bit counts increased by 100-300 within 15 minutes on peers; link_state metric oscillated between 2 (down) and 4 (up/active) with rapid transitions. dmesg snippets included repeated lines: "NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus" and "nvlink: link 1 status change: FLAPPING". nvidia-smi topo -m showed transient topology changes while link flaps occurred. Firmware versions on the three nodes differ: gpu-cc-15 running NVSwitch fw 1.3.2 (new), gpu-cc-14 & 18 on 1.2.9. Driver version across nodes: 535.86.05. No consistent temperature or power-supply alerts in iDRAC logs; BMC temps nominal. Observed slightly elevated PCIe re-train counters (AER) on one host.
quick_mitigations: 1) Drain affected node (kubectl cordon + drain --ignore-daemonsets) and move long-running jobs off immediately. 2) If link flap persists, stop inference worker processes to lower inter-GPU traffic (systemctl stop redwood-inference-worker). 3) Short-term: restart NVIDIA driver (sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo modprobe -r nvidia_drm nvidia_uvm nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia) — note: this is disruptive to active workloads. 4) If firmware mismatch suspected between NVSwitch peers, prefer rolling nodes back to the last-known-stable NVSwitch firmware (see rollback_checklist). 5) Apply temporary routing rule in the serving gateway to prefer non-interconnected-GPU allocations for high cross-GPU traffic routes until stable.
rollback_checklist:
- Confirm target firmware version (locked stable = 1.2.9 for now). - Open maint window: ~20 minutes per node. - Ensure node is drained and powered on (watch for pending jobs). - Pull NVSwitch firmware package id: fw_nvlink_1.2.9.tar.gz from internal-artifacts (sha256:abc123). - Command sequence (run as root): 
  1) sudo nvlink-fw-tool --status 
  2) sudo nvlink-fw-tool --apply /opt/fw/fw_nvlink_1.2.9.tar.gz --force --reboot-after 
  3) wait for node to reboot, verify with sudo nvlink-fw-tool --status == 1.2.9 
  4) restart driver and our services, run stress-check (python tools/gpu/topo-checker.py --smoke) 
- Post-rollback health checks: no link_state flaps for 30 minutes under 75% traffic. - If rollback fails or link flaps continue, escalate to Nvidia field engineer and open an RMA for suspected hardware NVSwitch defect.
followups: - Ask firmware owners to gate NVSwitch upgrades across the fleet with a canary pool and telemetry baseline (owner: Lina Chen). - Add a Prometheus rule to detect high-frequency link_state transitions (>5 flips in 10m) and page oncall. - Plan: schedule a controlled repro in lab with traffic generator (owner: Rohan Patel) to exercise NVLink with fw 1.3.2 vs 1.2.9. - Create a small automation to auto-drain nodes showing >2 link flips in 5m (owner: Diego Alvarez). - Run a kernel/driver regression test suite against driver 535.86.05 on our CI hardware matrix. - Postmortem write-up if reoccurs; potential RCA: firmware-induced signal retraining under load or driver/firmware handshake regression.
notes_to_self: - When restarting driver, capture full /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and dmesg -T pre/post restart. - Prefer sequence: drain -> nvlink-fw downgrade -> driver restart -> smoke tests -> uncordon. - Avoid full powercycle unless nvlink-fw-tool indicates unsafe state. - Keep capacity reserve during maintenance windows (limit rolling work to 10% of fleet). - Tag incident JIRA and link back to this doc for iteration.
action_items: Lina Chen: Gate NVSwitch upgrades + telemetry baseline by 2026-01-10
Rohan Patel: Build repro traffic harness and run comparisons for fw 1.3.2 vs 1.2.9 by 2025-12-12
Diego Alvarez: Prototype autoremediation (auto-drain) and PR for ops-runbook by 2025-12-09
extras:
Useful commands: 
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,index,uuid,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,clocks.gr --format=csv -l 5 
- nvidia-smi nvlink --query-link=link_id,link_state,link_speed --format=csv 
- sudo nvlink-fw-tool --status 
- journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced --since '1 hour ago' 
- check AER: sudo ethtool -S pci0000:65:00.0 | grep aerr
Remember to snapshot /var/log and upload to S3 before any driver/firmware changes.
